# costfluent_allocation_rule (Resource)

Manages a Costfluent allocation rule: which cost belongs to which segment. Needs a token with `manageCostAllocation`, `viewCostAllocation` and `viewCosts` on the workspace.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "costfluent_workspace" "production" {
  name     = "Production"
  currency = "USD"
}

resource "costfluent_segment" "checkout_platform" {
  workspace_id = costfluent_workspace.production.id

  team_label  = "Checkout"
  product     = "Checkout"
  cost_centre = "CC-1001"
}

# Every EC2 cost row in Frankfurt belongs to the checkout segment. The filter is CQL text, or the
# cost filter's JSON document built with jsonencode, as costfluent_cost_report takes it.
resource "costfluent_allocation_rule" "checkout_compute" {
  workspace_id = costfluent_workspace.production.id
  name         = "Checkout compute in Frankfurt"
  priority     = 10

  filter = "costs.service = 'AmazonEC2' AND costs.region = 'eu-central-1'"

  segment_id = costfluent_segment.checkout_platform.id
}

# A lower-priority fallback: the rest of the cost in resource groups named checkout-*.
resource "costfluent_allocation_rule" "checkout_by_resource_group" {
  workspace_id = costfluent_workspace.production.id
  name         = "Checkout resource groups"
  priority     = 20

  filter = jsonencode([{ field = "ResourceGroup", operator = "StartsWith", values = ["checkout-"] }])

  segment_id = costfluent_segment.checkout_platform.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `filter` (String) The cost this rule claims, as the cost filter's JSON document (build it with jsonencode) or as CQL text, as costfluent_cost_report takes it. It must constrain at least one dimension and may not read a virtual tag.
- `name` (String) Rule name. Documentation only; it moves no cost.
- `segment_id` (String) Segment token this rule assigns cost to.
- `workspace_id` (String) Workspace token the rule belongs to.

### Optional

- `is_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule claims cost. A disabled rule affects no total, so this is how a mapping is staged before it moves anyone's numbers.
- `priority` (Number) Evaluation order; lower wins. Ties break by creation time, so the order is total and stable. Leave gaps: inserting a rule ahead of another then needs no renumbering.

### Read-Only

- `cost_centre` (String) The segment's cost centre, echoed for readability.
- `cost_kind` (String) Direct or Shared, following the segment. Not settable: a rule and its segment disagreeing about whether cost is shared is not a state to ask for.
- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp.
- `id` (String) Allocation rule token.
- `segment_name` (String) The segment name, echoed for readability.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update timestamp.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A allocation rule is imported by "<workspace ID>:<allocation rule ID>"; the workspace is required.
terraform import costfluent_allocation_rule.checkout_by_tag wsp_0000000000000000000001:alr_0000000000000000000001
```
